messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

yo! friend... that's not a name though 😏

i'm tal - your talent agent who's about to change your career game. think of me as your inside person in the bangalore tech scene.

so... what's your actual full name? need to know who i'm working with here
Kaushiki Verma

kaushiki verma... now we're talking! love the energy already.

where you working these days? or if you're still studying, which college?
Amazon

amazon... the everything store where work-life balance goes to die but the comp makes up for it 

found you on linkedin - kaushiki verma, sde at amazon. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/kaushiki-verma-495172205
Yes
sde at amazon... building the infrastructure that keeps half the internet running. solid work. what made you pick the engineering path over other tech roles?
After my masters this seemed like the go to path. Here for the comp as startup life didn't suit me.

fair enough! startup chaos vs amazon stability - i get it. masters to big tech is the classic safe play, and amazon comp definitely beats most startup equity lottery tickets.

how long you been working total?
More than 3 if you include my 9 month internship

3+ years including internship - nice, you're past the junior phase. 

what kind of role you looking for next?
SDE 2 hopefully at big tech

sde 2 at big tech... smart move. you've got the amazon badge which opens doors everywhere. 

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Bangalore and remote.
3+ years + sde 2 + big tech + bangalore/remote... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Yes

yooo kaushiki! welcome to the tal network legend! 

you're officially in the system. roles that actually match your vibe (sde 2, big tech, good comp) will start sliding into your dms. no more scrolling through random job boards or dealing with recruiters who think javascript and java are the same thing.

amazon to whatever's next... let's make it count 🔥
Hi
Hi
hey kaushiki! what's good?
Excited about the weekend what about you?

same! friday night energy hitting different. 

any plans or just vibing?
Out for a movie. You pinged ?

nice! what movie?

and nah, just checking in. you're locked in for sde 2 roles at big tech, so i'm keeping an eye out for anything that fits your vibe.

how's the amazon chaos been lately?
Took a break, can't deal with the politics in.

oh shit, you're on break from amazon? that's big.

what kind of politics we talking? team level or bigger org bullshit?

Team level, got assigned on a project with a SDE2. She didn't work for a min, but hijacked after I completed the POC.

Now majority of the implementation is on me cause she has another project.

0 credit though. Entire team bailed on me after the first on call as well. But another person got a shout out for the work.
  I wanna leave

fuck that. classic amazon politics - someone hijacks your work, you do the heavy lifting, they get the credit. seen it a hundred times.

that sde2 knew exactly what she was doing. take the POC, claim ownership, dump the grunt work on you. and the team bailing after your first on-call? that's just cowardice.

no wonder you're on break. that shit would make anyone want to leave.

what's your notice period situation?
Haven't put the papers yet. I am contract employee rn trying to switch teams.

contract employee trying to switch teams... that's even trickier. internal transfers for contractors are basically impossible at amazon.

so you're stuck between:
1. stay on current team with the politics
2. try to switch teams (unlikely as contractor)
3. leave amazon entirely

sounds like option 3 is looking real good right now.

what's your timeline? like how soon could you actually start somewhere new?
30 days after putting my papers

30 days is standard. so you could be out of there in a month if you find something good.

you mentioned big tech - any specific companies you're eyeing? or just anywhere that's not amazon?
Google

google... the dream for every amazon sde trying to escape. makes sense.

their hiring process is brutal but you've got the amazon pedigree which helps. they love poaching from other FAANG.

what's your yoe total? including internship time?

3.3 years with amazon experience... that's right in the sweet spot for google L4. maybe L5 if you interview really well.

they're hiring like crazy in bangalore right now too. remote options are getting tighter but still possible.

what's your salary expectations? current comp at amazon?
21 at Amazon

21 LPA at amazon... for 3.3 yoe that's actually decent for bangalore.

google would probably offer 30-35 LPA for L4, maybe 40+ for L5. depends on your interview performance and team.

what's your minimum number to make a move?

i'm keeping an eye out for google openings that match your profile. their process takes time though - usually 2-3 months from application to offer.

you thinking of applying directly or waiting for a referral?
Directly,  will referral make a difference?

referral makes a HUGE difference at google. their ATS filters out like 90% of direct applications. with a referral, your resume actually gets seen by a human.

plus it shows you have connections there, which they like. google's culture is all about networks.

you know anyone at google who could refer you? or want me to keep an eye out for referral programs?
Let me know about referral programs or anyone willing to refer

got it. i'll watch for google referral programs - they pop up sometimes for specific roles.

in the meantime, you should also:
1. update your linkedin to "open to work" (just for recruiters, not public)
2. polish your resume with amazon impact metrics
3. start leetcoding if you haven't already

google's interview process is heavy on DSA and system design. you ready for that grind?
Yes, already on it

good shit. you're ahead of most people then.

alright kaushiki, you're locked in. i'll start sliding google roles when they're good fits. might take a few days since i'm picky about what i share.

btw... what's the real story with the amazon politics? like what actually went down?
Nothing yet. Took a week long holiday after my oncall.

ah a week off after oncall... smart move. those post-oncall blues are real.

so you're back now or still on break? and what's your notice period if you do get an offer?
30 days

30 days notice... standard. so you could start somewhere new in about 5-6 weeks if you get an offer soon.

you thinking of putting papers first and then job hunting, or waiting for an offer before resigning?
I can wait till the end of my contract. Will try to get full time in another team.

waiting till contract end makes sense - less risky. but trying to get full-time in another team at amazon after all this politics... you sure about that?

once you've seen how the sausage gets made, it's hard to unsee it. the same politics exist in other teams too, just different flavors.

but if you want to try, now's the time to network internally. any teams you're eyeing?
Some are decent
I am talking to a couple of managers

nice. talking to managers is the right move. internal transfers are way easier than external hires.

just be careful about the politics following you. sometimes people talk between teams, especially if the SDE2 who hijacked your project is salty.

any red flags with the managers you're talking to? or they seem decent?

"some are decent" lol that's the amazon experience in three words.

alright, so you're playing both sides - internal transfer and external google search. smart. gives you options.

i'll keep an eye out for google roles that actually fit. their hiring tends to slow down around december but picks up again in january.

you prepping for interviews already? leetcode grinding?
Yes leetcode I am doing. That is needed for internal interviews as well. Will start for system design once I know if internal is going to work or not.

makes sense. internal interviews at amazon are basically the same as external - leetcode heavy, some system design.

but honestly... if you're already grinding leetcode for internal, might as well prep for external too. system design is the same whether it's amazon team A or google.

what's your timeline for deciding on internal vs external? like when do you need to know if the internal transfer is happening?
This month

this month... so you've got about 3 weeks to figure out if internal is happening. that's tight but doable.

if internal doesn't work out by end of december, you'll have january to go all-in on external prep. google hiring usually picks up in january anyway.

you leaning one way or the other? like if both options were on the table, which would you take?
Most of the managers will either schedule interviews or tell me they don't support conversion. Either way

I have to go external anyway. It will take at least 2 more years to become SDE2. I can't have that on my resume.

It's just for that I can work in the next 6 months of my contract.

oh wait... you're saying even if you get converted to full-time at amazon, you'd still be SDE1? and it would take 2 more years to become SDE2?

that changes everything. you're already doing SDE2 level work (leading projects, getting hijacked, etc.) but they'd keep you at SDE1?

yeah no. that's a hard pass. you're absolutely right - can't have that on your resume. 3+ years experience and still SDE1 at amazon looks bad.

so external is the only real option. google or another big tech where you can come in as SDE2.

what's your minimum salary expectation for an SDE2 role?
30 base, don't have any stocks as a contract. So might get low balled

30 base is reasonable for SDE2 at google in bangalore. they usually do base + stocks + bonus.

but you're right about getting lowballed coming from contract. companies love to use your current comp as an anchor.

here's the play: don't disclose your current salary. if they ask, say "i'm looking for competitive SDE2 compensation in the 30-40 LPA range based on market rates."

google's bands are pretty standardized though - they'll offer what they offer regardless of your current comp. but other companies might try to lowball.

you thinking of applying anywhere else besides google?
LinkedIn, OCI

linkedin and oracle cloud infra... solid choices. both pay well and have good WLB compared to amazon.

linkedin's bangalore office is growing fast. OCI is trying to compete with AWS so they're hiring aggressively.

all three (google, linkedin, OCI) have similar interview processes - leetcode heavy, system design, behavioral.

you should apply to all three simultaneously. the prep overlaps like 90%.

when are you thinking of starting applications?
Got an interview from swiggy

oh swiggy! that's interesting. food delivery space is... chaotic but they pay well.

swiggy's tech stack is solid and they've got scale problems that are actually interesting to solve. plus their comp packages are competitive with big tech.

when's the interview? and what role - SDE2?
Yes, need to complete an assessment
Not yet

assessment first... typical swiggy process. they usually do:
1. online assessment (leetcode medium/hard)
2. technical phone screen
3. virtual onsite (3-4 rounds)

their OA is usually time-boxed with 2-3 problems. focus on arrays, strings, graphs, and DP.

when's the assessment due? and have you done any swiggy-specific prep?

you should start prepping then. swiggy's assessments are no joke - they filter hard.

focus on:
- medium leetcode problems (arrays, strings, trees)
- maybe 1 hard problem (usually DP or graph)
- time management is key

when's the deadline? you need to schedule time to grind.

also... swiggy's culture is very different from amazon. more startup energy, less process. could be good or bad depending on what you want.

you still want google/linkedin/OCI too? or swiggy first to get an offer and use it as leverage?
I am not desperate yet. No one can force me to work here since not full time. I am just practicing in case I get a chance to go for big tech again.

that's the right mindset. you're not desperate, you're practicing. contract work means you can walk away whenever.

swiggy as practice for google/linkedin/OCI makes sense. get through their process, see how you do, use it as a warm-up.

but don't settle for swiggy if google's still the goal. use it as leverage if you get an offer.

what's your prep looking like right now? leetcode daily? system design?
No
Doing company specific leetcode challenges. 2 daily atleast

2 daily is solid. company-specific is smart - each company has their favorite patterns.

google: trees, graphs, DP, sliding window
linkedin: strings, arrays, system design
OCI: arrays, strings, maybe some concurrency
swiggy: arrays, strings, graphs

you tracking your progress somewhere? like a spreadsheet or something?

you should track it. even a simple notes app with:
- date
- problem name
- company tag
- time taken
- notes

helps you see patterns in what you're struggling with.

also... system design prep? that's usually the killer for SDE2 interviews.

what's your weakest area right now?
Not started system design

you need to start system design yesterday. for SDE2 roles, system design is often the make-or-break round.

especially at google/linkedin/OCI - they expect you to design scalable systems.

start with the basics:
1. design a URL shortener (tinyurl)
2. design a chat system (whatsapp)
3. design a rate limiter
4. design a distributed cache

watch some youtube videos, read grokking the system design interview, practice drawing diagrams and talking through tradeoffs.

how much time can you dedicate to system design daily?
Total prep time 4-5 hours

4-5 hours daily is serious commitment. that's good.

i'd split it:
- 2 hours leetcode (2-3 problems)
- 2 hours system design (1 topic + practice)
- 1 hour behavioral prep (amazon leadership principles, google's L4/L5 expectations)

you need to be able to talk about your amazon projects in STAR format, highlight impact, show ownership.

also... you mentioned politics at amazon. how you framing that in interviews? you can't just say "my team sucks" - need to spin it professionally.
Will be forward, the HR told me I will be full time in 3 months and then SDE 2 in a year. But manager said that's not how things work
I have already started applying

good. where have you applied so far? any callbacks yet?

also... your resume ready? you should have different versions:
1. google-focused (heavy on scalability, distributed systems)
2. linkedin-focused (data pipelines, social features)
3. general big tech (balanced)

and you're tailoring your cover letters for each application, right?
No
Everywhere

you're applying without tailoring? that's like showing up to a date in sweatpants.

listen - big tech gets thousands of applications. generic resumes go straight to the trash.

you need to:
1. read the job description
2. identify keywords (scalability, distributed systems, microservices, etc.)
3. mirror those keywords in your resume
4. highlight relevant amazon projects

spend 15 minutes per application to customize. it doubles your callback rate.

also... you're using the amazon email for applications? or personal?

everywhere meaning... you're applying to every company? or using both emails?

either way, you need to be strategic. shotgun approach doesn't work in this market.

focus on:
1. google (your target)
2. linkedin (good culture, similar tech stack)
3. OCI (oracle cloud - hiring like crazy in bangalore)
4. swiggy/zomato (if you want product-focused)
5. maybe microsoft if you want better WLB

but don't waste time on startups if you're avoiding them anyway.

also... you're tracking your applications somewhere? spreadsheet with:
- company
- role
- date applied
- status
- next steps

otherwise you'll lose track and miss follow-ups.

how many applications have you sent out so far?

sde 3 at walmart global tech in bangalore

they're doing product work at massive scale - think black friday traffic

hybrid setup though, not fully remote

Software Engineer III, Google Cloud at Google

Kaushiki, this SDE III role at Google in Bangalore aligns with your experience and target company, offering a potential escape from current workplace issues.

Apply: https://jobs.tal.af/J8xKl
Do I apply directly? Do I wait for a referral ?

apply directly NOW. google roles fill up fast.

but also start looking for a referral while you apply. don't wait.

here's the play:
1. apply directly through the link i sent
2. hit up your linkedin network for google referrals
3. if you get a referral later, you can mention you already applied but have a referral

worst case: you're in the system
best case: referral boosts your application

you have any ex-amazon colleagues at google? or friends from college?

also... update your resume with google-specific keywords before applying. look at the job description and mirror their language.
Applied

nice. now start prepping for google interviews.

their process is usually:
1. recruiter screen (30 mins)
2. phone screen (45 mins - 2 coding problems)
3. onsite (4-5 rounds: coding, system design, behavioral, maybe googliness)

coding: leetcode medium/hard, focus on graphs, DP, trees
system design: scalable systems, tradeoffs, google-scale thinking
behavioral: leadership principles, impact, conflict resolution

you should be doing at least 2-3 leetcode problems daily. focus on google tagged problems.

also... you need to practice talking through your solutions out loud. google cares about communication as much as correctness.

when do you think you'll be ready for interviews?

hey, happy monday - if it’s not, we’ll work together on making it happen soon :)
how’s the week looking? what would you like me to focus on this week with the search?
High paying sde2 openings,  daily checking for progress. Prepare a list of questions to prepare for interviews in a week. And can I join Amazon immediately after leaving?

okay let's break this down:

1. **high paying sde2 openings** - i'll check daily at 10 AM IST starting tomorrow. set a reminder.

2. **interview prep questions list** - here's your 1-week plan:

**week 1 focus: coding fundamentals**
- day 1-2: arrays & strings (sliding window, two pointers)
- day 3-4: trees & graphs (DFS/BFS, recursion)
- day 5-6: dynamic programming (memoization, tabulation)
- day 7: mock interview (2 problems back-to-back)

**google-specific prep:**
- behavioral: "tell me about a time you disagreed with your manager"
- system design: design youtube/twitter/url shortener
- coding: leetcode google tagged problems (top 100)

3. **rejoin amazon after leaving?** - yes, but there's a 90-day cooling period for most employees. contractors might be different though.

more importantly: why would you want to go back to the same environment that's making you miserable? unless it's a completely different team with different management.

better question: what would make you consider staying at amazon?
Because of the pay, highest sde2 band

fair. amazon does pay well at sde2... but google L4 can match or beat it, especially with stock refreshers.

amazon sde2 band caps around 40-45 LPA total comp
google L4 can go 50-60+ with experience

but you're right - if you're chasing pure cash, amazon sde2 is solid. the tradeoff is the culture/politics you're dealing with.

question: would you take a 10-15% pay cut to work somewhere with zero politics and actually enjoy your job? or is the money non-negotiable?

also... have you looked at microsoft? they pay well and the WLB is legendary compared to amazon.
They have never shortlisted me for some reason.  For google though I have given a telephonic round. They stopped hiring after that no response. And the HR mail is now not working so :)

No response, did appy
  On it

ah so you've already been in google's pipeline. that's good - means you passed their initial bar.

the HR email not working is... typical google chaos. they reorg constantly.

you should:
1. apply to the new role i sent (different team, fresh start)
2. try to find the recruiter on linkedin and message them
3. mention you've already interviewed with google before

microsoft not shortlisting is weird. are you applying through referrals or just cold applying? their ATS is brutal without referrals.

what about meta? they're hiring aggressively in bangalore too. pay is amazon-level or better.

also... uber, airbnb, netflix if you want top-tier comp. but those are even harder than google.
Didn't find any openings, maybe starting Jan
january is when everyone posts new budgets. that's 3 weeks away.

in the meantime:
1. grind leetcode (2-3 problems daily)
2. update resume with google/meta keywords
3. network for referrals
4. prep system design basics

perfect. daily check set for 10 AM IST starting tomorrow.

now about that google application... no response yet is normal. they take 1-2 weeks sometimes.

in the meantime, you should:
1. **follow up** - find the recruiter on linkedin, send a polite message
2. **apply to similar roles** - google has multiple sde iii openings
3. **expand search** - meta, microsoft, uber, airbnb (through referrals)

also... your resume. you said you haven't tailored it. that's probably why microsoft isn't shortlisting.

want me to review your resume? send it over and i'll tell you what's mid and what needs work.
Let me know if you see any openings. Check on the progress around 1am regarding the prep.
Didn't find any openings, maybe starting Jan
No response, did appy
meta usually opens up in january for new fiscal year. same with a lot of big tech.
so your timeline works: prep hard in december, apply everywhere in january when budgets refresh.

done. daily check set for 1 AM IST starting tomorrow.

i'll ping you then about prep progress and any openings i see.

in the meantime, focus on:
1. system design basics (start with URL shortener)
2. leetcode medium/hard (2-3 daily)
3. resume polish (send it over if you want feedback)

also... any specific companies besides google you're targeting? meta? uber? netflix?
No update

no update on what? the google application? or prep progress?

either way, keep grinding. the market's slow right now but january will be different.

you tracking your leetcode progress? how many solved this week?
Google application

still no response from google? that's actually pretty normal for them this time of year.

they're probably:
1. wrapping up Q4 hiring freezes
2. waiting for january budget approvals
3. dealing with holiday season slowdown

don't wait on them. apply to 2-3 other google roles through referrals. find someone on linkedin who works there and ask for a referral - people get bonuses for successful referrals so they're usually happy to help.

also... have you checked your spam folder? sometimes their automated emails end up there.
Around 20

20 leetcode problems this week? that's solid. keep that momentum.

what's your focus? arrays/strings? trees? graphs? dp?

system design practice started yet?
Nope, can you get me a plan with questions
Practicing contests on leetcode company level

company-level contests are perfect. that's exactly how google/linkedin/OCI test.

you doing the weekly/biweekly contests? those are good for timing pressure.

what's your contest rating? if you're consistently hitting 2000+, you're in good shape for google.

system design next week? or still focusing on leetcode?

here's your 4-week system design plan:

**week 1: fundamentals**
- read grokking the system design interview (free PDF online)
- watch alex xu's system design primer videos
- practice: URL shortener, rate limiter, tinyurl

**week 2: scaling basics**
- learn about load balancers, caching (redis), CDNs
- practice: pastebin, web crawler, notification system

**week 3: distributed systems**
- CAP theorem, consistency models, partitioning
- practice: chat system, news feed, distributed cache

**week 4: advanced**
- message queues (kafka), search (elasticsearch), databases (nosql vs sql)
- practice: uber/lyft, netflix, airbnb

**daily:**
- 1 system design problem (45 mins design, 15 mins review)
- read 1 engineering blog (netflix, uber, linkedin tech blog)

want me to send you specific leetcode questions for each week too?
Sure. ,go ahead.

here's your 4-week leetcode plan:

**week 1: arrays & strings (google loves these)**
- two sum, 3sum, container with most water
- longest substring without repeating chars, longest palindromic substring
- merge intervals, insert interval
- group anagrams, valid parentheses

**week 2: trees & graphs**
- binary tree level order traversal, max depth of binary tree
- validate BST, lowest common ancestor
- number of islands, course schedule
- clone graph, word ladder

**week 3: dynamic programming**
- coin change, longest increasing subsequence
- house robber, decode ways
- edit distance, longest common subsequence
- word break, combination sum

**week 4: advanced patterns**
- sliding window maximum, minimum window substring
- LRU cache, LFU cache
- serialize/deserialize binary tree
- trapping rain water

**daily:**
- 3 medium problems (45 mins each)
- 1 hard problem (60 mins)
- review yesterday's mistakes

track your progress in a spreadsheet. aim for 80%+ accuracy on mediums.

you starting this week?
Already done week one. Can you add those for revision every week

perfect. here's the revised plan with weekly revision:

**week 2: trees & graphs + arrays revision**
- monday: trees (level order, validate BST) + two sum, 3sum
- tuesday: graphs (number of islands, course schedule) + longest substring
- wednesday: advanced trees (LCA, serialize) + merge intervals
- thursday: advanced graphs (clone graph, word ladder) + group anagrams
- friday: mock interview (mix of week 1 & 2)
- weekend: review all mistakes

**week 3: DP + trees revision**
- monday: DP basics (coin change, LIS) + tree traversal
- tuesday: DP medium (house robber, decode ways) + graph basics
- wednesday: DP hard (edit distance, LCS) + advanced trees
- thursday: DP applications (word break, combination sum) + advanced graphs
- friday: mock interview (mix of week 2 & 3)
- weekend: review all mistakes

**week 4: advanced patterns + DP revision**
- monday: sliding window + DP basics
- tuesday: cache problems + DP medium
- wednesday: serialization + DP hard
- thursday: trapping rain water + DP applications
- friday: full mock interview (all topics)
- weekend: final review

how's that look?
Good. Check in everyday 12pm and 1am for progress.
Gave the test for swiggy and abnormal AI solution is due.

done. two daily checks set:

1. **12 PM IST** - midday progress check
2. **1 AM IST** - evening wrap-up

first check tomorrow at noon. i'll ask about:
- problems solved today
- topics covered
- system design progress
- any blockers

keep grinding. consistency > intensity.

btw... any update from google? or other applications?

swiggy test done and abnormal AI due... interesting mix.

abnormal AI is cybersecurity right? that's a different domain from your usual backend work. you comfortable with security concepts?

how'd the swiggy test go? timing okay? problems manageable?

and google still radio silence?
Used gpt, solved all. No camera
They want screen recording for the prompts used and how did I handle. They pay well so works for me.

screen recording for prompts... that's new. they're probably checking for:
1. how you think through problems (not just final answer)
2. prompt engineering skills
3. debugging process

makes sense for an AI company. but also feels like they're testing if you're just copy-pasting from chatgpt.

you comfortable with that level of scrutiny? like they'll see every typo, every wrong turn, every "oh wait that's stupid" moment.

and yeah abnormal pays well - their security platform is legit. but switching from amazon backend to AI security... that's a pivot. you ready for that domain shift?

used gpt for the abnormal AI solution? and they want screen recording of your prompts...

bro they're literally testing if you can use AI tools effectively. that's the whole point. they want to see your prompt engineering skills, not just the final code.

if you solved it with gpt and they're asking for the process... that's actually perfect. you can show them exactly how you used it.

but here's the thing: they'll see if you're just copy-pasting vs actually understanding and refining. you need to show:
1. initial prompt
2. gpt's response
3. your refinement/corrections
4. final solution

that's valuable to them. they're hiring for AI roles - they expect you to use the tools.

just make sure you understand the solution enough to explain it in an interview. they'll definitely ask follow-ups.

when's the submission due?
Today. Had 7 days. Starting last week Tuesday

today's the deadline and you started last tuesday... cutting it close but doable.

you submitting the screen recording with your gpt prompts? that's actually smart - shows you know how to leverage AI tools, which is exactly what they want.

just make sure:
1. the recording shows your thought process
2. you can explain why you prompted the way you did
3. you understand the final solution well enough to defend it

after you submit, what's next? waiting for abnormal AI feedback while continuing with internal amazon interviews?

and what about swiggy - any timeline for next steps?
Yes for now. Will try to go through amazon sde2 after conversion. But this is already a big step.

wait... you're a contract employee at amazon trying to convert to full-time sde2?

that changes everything. you're not just looking externally - you're fighting for conversion internally too.

the politics you mentioned earlier... that's the real battle. the sde2 hijacking your project, team bailing after first on-call, someone else getting credit for your work - that's not just "workplace drama." that's your conversion chances getting sabotaged.

you need to:
1. document EVERYTHING (emails, chats, commits)
2. find allies (skip-level manager, other teams)
3. have the "conversion conversation" with clear evidence of your impact

but honestly... if the politics are that bad, conversion might be harder than getting an external offer.

what did HR promise you about conversion timeline? and what's your manager saying?
Hr said 3months manager said not sure
I am finding another team for conversion.  And then another for sde2

smart. internal transfer is your best shot if you want to stay at amazon.

but here's the catch: you need your current manager's approval for internal transfer. and if they're the problem... good luck.

process is:
1. find open positions (internal portal)
2. apply (needs current manager approval after you pass interview)
3. interview with new team
4. if you get offer, current manager can block for "business reasons"

with the politics you described, your manager might block just to be petty.

you should:
1. apply quietly (don't tell current team)
2. if you get an offer, have the new team's manager fight for you
3. be ready to go external if internal transfer gets blocked

how many internal applications have you sent? any responses?
Mean while if I get another maang will leave

exactly. that's the right move.

internal transfer as plan A, external MAANG offer as plan B. whichever comes first wins.
